title: bug: NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP tells agent seats to call moe.join_team, which their tools/list hides
description:
Observed 2026-10-30 in an interactive architect session (architect-32ff5555):
- The seat had teamId null, while every other architect, QA and most workers were on team-a94dc136bb2b49c2aa8df6977c354696.
- In-session moe.claim_next_task {statuses:['PLANNING']} returned hasNext:false, code NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP, with nextAction moe.join_team. Six unassigned PLANNING tasks sat in epic-be924fb8, and architect-4ae016fb held that epic's PLANNING column.
- The agent could not follow the nextAction. TOOL_AUDIENCE in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/index.ts maps 'moe.join_team' and 'moe.list_teams' to [], so toolsForRole hides them from the architect, worker and QA tools/list.
- The wrapper's pre-claim join retry (scripts/moe-agent.sh, around line 2082) only runs between CLI sessions, never for claims made inside an interactive session.
- util/teamMembershipHeal.ts only heals tombstoned former members.
Net effect: the session's only recourse is to end early.

Deliverable: an agent seat refused for missing team membership gets a remedy it can actually execute. Two options:
- name a role-visible action, e.g. 'end the session; the wrapper retries moe.join_team before its next claim';
- or have the claim path heal a teamless seat into its role team, as the wrapper would.
The planner picks one.

NOT in scope: changing the solo epic+status rule or the TOOL_AUDIENCE policy for other tools.

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: A NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP refusal served to an architect, worker or qa caller names only actions that caller can take: no tool missing from toolsForRole(role). New vitest cases assert this for each of the three roles.
Existing teamMembershipHeal and solo epic+status rule tests pass unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
RED TESTS FIRST (DoD 1). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/noTeamMembershipAudience.test.ts and run it red against the current code before touching runtime.

Fixture (copy the ToolTestHarness pattern from claimNextTask.test.ts 'moe.claim_next_task — execution attempts'): `const h = new ToolTestHarness(); beforeEach(() => { h.init(); h.setupMoeFolder(); h.createEpic(); }); afterEach(() => h.cleanup());`. Imports: claimNextTaskTool (./claimNextTask.js), waitForTaskTool (./waitForTask.js), getTools + toolsForRole (./index.js), ToolTestHarness (./toolTestHarness.js), noTeamMembershipRefusal (../util/teamMembershipHeal.js), type TeamRole (../types/schema.js).

SEATS = [{ role: 'architect', status: 'PLANNING' }, { role: 'worker', status: 'WORKING' }, { role: 'qa', status: 'REVIEW' }] — each seat claims from its own column. Solo-blocked board per role (the exact shape that arms the solo epic+status rule): `h.createTask({ id: 'task-free', status, order: 1 })`, `h.createTask({ id: 'task-peer', status, order: 2, assignedWorkerId: `${role}-peer` })`, `h.createWorker({ id: `${role}-peer`, currentTaskId: 'task-peer', status: 'CODING' })`, `h.createWorker({ id: `${role}-solo` })` (harness default teamId null), then `await h.state.load()`.

Helpers: `namedTools(reply)` = the distinct `moe.<name>` tokens in JSON.stringify(reply) (regex /moe\.[a-z_]+/g), which covers nextAction.tool, its args and every line of prose; `visible(role)` = toolsForRole(getTools(h.state), role).map((t) => t.name).

Enumerated test cases (each assertion is required; a truthiness check is not enough):
- T1-T3 (one per SEATS row, it.each or a loop): claim_next_task, called as `claimNextTaskTool(h.state).handler({ workerId: `${role}-solo`, statuses: [status] }, h.state)`. Assert (a) the premise, so the case cannot pass vacuously: visible(role) contains neither 'moe.join_team' nor 'moe.list_teams'; (b) reply.hasNext === false and reply.code === 'NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP'; (c) reply.nextAction is undefined; (d) reply.sessionHandoff toEqual { action: 'END_SESSION', workerId: `${role}-solo`, reason: expect.stringContaining(`${role}-solo`) }, so a taskId key or another addressee fails; (e) THE DoD-1 ASSERTION: namedTools(reply).filter((t) => !visible(role).includes(t)) toEqual [], so the failure lists any hidden tool; (f) JSON.stringify(reply) does not contain 'taken by concurrent workers'; (g) the solo rule still refused and nothing healed: h.state.getTask('task-free')!.assignedWorkerId is null and h.state.getTeamForWorker(`${role}-solo`) is null.
- T4-T6 (same board per role): the wait_for_task immediate path, `waitForTaskTool(h.state).handler({ workerId: `${role}-solo`, statuses: [status], timeoutMs: 1000 }, h.state)`, with the same (b)-(f) plus reply.timedOut undefined (it answers at once and never parks).
- T7 control, for callers whose tools/list shows moe.join_team: for [['governor-solo', 'governor'], ['w-solo', null]], refusal = noTeamMembershipRefusal(id). Assert nextAction.tool === 'moe.join_team', nextAction.args toEqual { workerId: id }, sessionHandoff undefined, and namedTools(refusal) is a subset of toolsForRole(getTools(h.state), role). Governor goes through the pure function because claim_next_task redirects a governor-prefixed caller to moe.enter_governance before the solo rule (claimNextTask.ts, the resolveWorkerRole === 'governor' branch near line 341).
- T8 pure function, per seat role: noTeamMembershipRefusal(`${role}-x`) has no nextAction, and its sessionHandoff is { action: 'END_SESSION', workerId: `${role}-x` } with a string reason. This pins the one function all three producers share (claimNextTask.ts:712, waitForTask.ts:310 and the subscription wake at waitForTask.ts:441), so the wake producer, which these tests do not drive, cannot drift.

Run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/noTeamMembershipAudience.test.ts`. T1-T6 and T8 must FAIL on the current code (moe.join_team is named; there is no sessionHandoff), and T7 must PASS. Paste the red summary into the complete_step note.

All 9 failures are 'expected { tool: moe.join_team, … } to be undefined' on nextAction: architect/worker/qa × (claim_next_task, wait_for_task immediate path, pure noTeamMembershipRefusal). Passing: 3 premise cases (tools/list hides moe.join_team and moe.list_teams for each seat role) and the 2 control cases (governor-solo, w-solo keep the join_team nextAction, no handoff, only visible tools). implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT the role-aware refusal (runtime + the one superseded test assertion pair + stale comments). Turn step 1 green.

1) packages/moe-daemon/src/util/teamMembershipHeal.ts
- Import roleFromWorkerId from './workerRole.js'. That module is util-to-util and has type-only imports, so no import cycle. Do NOT import tools/index.ts: tools/index.ts -> claimNextTask.ts -> this module would form a cycle.
- Add `export interface NoTeamMembershipHandoff { hasNext: false; code: typeof NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP; sessionHandoff: { action: 'END_SESSION'; workerId: string; reason: string } }`. It has no taskId, because no task is involved.
- noTeamMembershipRefusal(workerId: string) now returns NoTeamMembershipRefusal | NoTeamMembershipHandoff. Keep the signature single-argument and pure, so none of the three call sites changes.
  - When roleFromWorkerId(workerId) is 'architect', 'worker' or 'qa' (non-null and not 'governor'), return the handoff variant with NO nextAction.
  - Suggested reason, refine freely: `Worker ${workerId} belongs to no team, and every claimable candidate sits in an epic+status a live worker already holds. A team may work one epic+status in parallel; a solo worker may not, so the queue is not empty and nothing raced you: your team membership is missing. This session cannot fix that, because joining a team is the launcher's job. Save any handoff, then end this session; before its next claim the wrapper retries the team join and reports why it fails (for example a full team).`
  - Hard constraints on that reason: it names NO moe.* tool at all, and it keeps none of the concurrent-claim wording.
  - Every other caller keeps today's join_team object byte-for-byte. That means a governor, a role-less id such as 'w-solo', the IDE and scripts/moe-call.sh. util/teamMembershipHeal.test.ts pins that shape and must pass unchanged.
- Rewrite the function's docstring to say why the id prefix is the whole story. This refusal is served only to a caller with no team, live or tombstoned (resolveEffectiveTeam returned null). For such a caller, McpAdapter's tools/list role (resolveWorkerRole) falls back to roleFromWorkerId. TOOL_AUDIENCE lists moe.join_team and moe.list_teams to no architect, worker or qa seat, while toolsForRole shows the governor every non-wrapper tool.
- One more docstring line on who acts on the handoff:
  - the moe-account-switch mod ends an interactive TUI on any top-level END_SESSION addressed to its MOE_WORKER_ID (scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/hooks/register.ts endSessionInstruction);
  - both wrappers key only on code === 'NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP' (moe-agent.sh claim_refused_no_team; moe-agent.ps1 near line 1498) and re-run the team join before their next claim.
- Error handling: the function stays total and never throws. An empty or unprefixed id (roleFromWorkerId needs the trailing dash, so 'architectX' is unprefixed) takes the join_team branch. A claim or wait can never fail because its refusal was built.

2) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForTask.ts: COMMENTS ONLY, no code. Three comments still promise a join_team nextAction:
- the MatchResult.skippedForNoTeam docstring ('...with NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP and a join_team nextAction...');
- the findMatchingTask tail ('...report it so the caller reaches join_team');
- the immediate-path comment above `return noTeamMembershipRefusal(workerId)` ('...with the code and the join_team nextAction...').
Reword each to say the caller gets claim_next_task's NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP remedy for its role.

3) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForTask.test.ts. This is the DoD 1 vs DoD 2 reconciliation; touch nothing else.
- The test 'does NOT offer a task withheld by the solo-worker epic+status rule — and says WHY, exactly as claim_next_task does' waits as 'worker-b', a worker seat by prefix. Its two remedy lines assert exactly what DoD 1 forbids for a worker caller: nextAction.tool === 'moe.join_team' and nextAction.args.workerId === 'worker-b'.
- Replace exactly those two lines with `expect(result.nextAction).toBeUndefined();` and `expect(result.sessionHandoff).toMatchObject({ action: 'END_SESSION', workerId: 'worker-b' });`.
- Reword the comment's 'with a join_team nextAction'.
- Keep every solo-rule assertion byte-identical: hasNext false, task undefined, code NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP, timedOut undefined.
- Edit no other test in any file.

Run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/noTeamMembershipAudience.test.ts src/tools/waitForTask.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts src/util/teamMembershipHeal.test.ts src/tools/toolAudience.test.ts`. It must be all green. Report all three files in complete_step modifiedFiles.

implementationPlan.description:
DOCUMENT the contract in docs/MCP_SERVER.md. NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP is undocumented today, and the claim reply's sessionHandoff line says 'resource-BLOCKED hold only'.

1) ### moe.claim_next_task, the **Returns** block:
- add `code?: "NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP"`;
- change the sessionHandoff line to `{ action: "END_SESSION", taskId?, workerId, reason }`, with the comment: resource-BLOCKED hold (taskId set), or NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP for an architect, worker or qa seat (no taskId): end this session;
- nextAction comment: absent on a resource-BLOCKED hold and on a seat's NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP;
- add 'moe.join_team' to the tool union, noted as NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP for a governor or role-less caller.

2) Add a **No team membership:** paragraph directly after the **Worker Constraint:** list.
- A claimer in no team (live, or remembered by a team's formerMemberIds tombstone) skips every candidate in an epic+status that a live other worker holds; a team may parallelize one. When that empties the pool, the answer is { hasNext: false, code: "NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP" }, never the concurrent-claim answer.
- The remedy follows what the caller's tools/list shows:
  - A worker id prefixed architect-, worker- or qa- has a tools/list that hides moe.join_team and moe.list_teams. It gets the END_SESSION handoff and no nextAction: save any handoff and end the session.
  - Both wrappers key on code and re-run the team join before their next claim, reporting a refused join (for example a full team). The moe-account-switch mod ends an interactive seat on the handoff.
  - A governor or a role-less caller (IDE, scripts/moe-call.sh, an unprefixed id) gets nextAction moe.join_team { workerId }.
- moe.wait_for_task answers the same refusal, either at once or when a matching task appears while it waits.

3) ### moe.wait_for_task **Returns**: add that NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP shape with its two variants.

4) The Claude Account Rotation paragraph (about line 2928) lists what carries END_SESSION: '(`moe.report_blocked` freeing it, or a claim refused over a resource-held task)'. Add: or a claim or wait refused for missing team membership.

Phrasing: write no sentence claiming the daemon never runs, touches or executes git; util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts greps docs for that.

Landing: five idle, unassigned WORKING CQ rows also declare this file (task-66e8d7d1, task-9cc13170, task-a9d1a74d, task-b621ddc9, task-ced85748), and it was clean at plan time.
- Make the edit through a wrapper-observed file-editing tool call. A shell redirect leaves no witness, so the default contested policy cannot credit it.
- A seat whose CLI has no such tool still lands the path while it was clean at that session's pre-flight and every contesting row is idle.
- If the session-ended line still reports it held (MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED), say so in the complete_task summary. Never hand-land it.

Architect note for worker and QA: DoD 1 vs DoD 2 reconciliation, decided at planning (TURBO).

DoD 2 says existing solo-rule tests pass unchanged. One of them cannot under DoD 1: the waitForTask.test.ts case 'does NOT offer a task withheld by the solo-worker epic+status rule — and says WHY, exactly as claim_next_task does'.
